medicalTaxCredit.title: Medical Expense Tax Credit Calculator
medicalTaxCredit.subtitle: Korean year-end tax settlement, tax year {year} · 15% of medical costs above 3% of your gross pay comes off your tax (20% for premature infants, 30% for infertility treatment)
medicalTaxCredit.salaryHint: Annual pay minus non-taxable allowances such as meal allowance. The 3% threshold is based on this amount.

expenses.title: Medical costs paid this year
expenses.hint: Enter only what you paid yourself between January 1 and December 31, {year}. Costs paid before you joined or after you left your job do not count.

family.label: Family aged 6 or under, 65 or over, or disabled
family.hint: No cap · 15%. Aged 6 or under on January 1, {year}; 65 or over on December 31, {year} (born in {birth} or earlier); disabled; or registered for severe, rare or tuberculosis care

general.label: Other family members (spouse, children, parents, etc.)
general.hint: Capped at 7M KRW a year · 15%. For dependants, what you pay counts regardless of their age or income.

premature.label: Premature infants and congenital conditions
premature.hint: No cap · 20%. Treatment recognized as needed because of premature birth, or treatment of a congenital condition

infertility.label: Infertility treatment
infertility.hint: No cap · 30%. Assisted reproduction such as IVF or IUI, plus related prescription drugs

insured.hint: Insurance payouts are subtracted from the medical cost they reimbursed. The simplified data service lists them per person.
insured.label: Insurance payout for {group}

medicalTaxCredit.capsNote: Enter glasses and contact lenses up to 500,000 KRW per person a year, and postpartum care centers up to 2M KRW per birth. Leave out cosmetic surgery, health supplements, caregiver fees and hospital bills abroad.

status.none: Enter your medical costs to see the credit and how much tax it saves.
status.threshold: Your medical costs do not exceed 3% of gross pay ({threshold} KRW), so there is nothing to credit.
status.noTax: The credit is {credit} KRW, but your tax due is already 0, so nothing comes back. If you are a dual-income couple, check your spouse below.
status.standard: The standard tax credit of 130,000 KRW beats the {credit} KRW medical credit, so the medical credit does not reduce your tax.
status.partial: The credit is {credit} KRW, but your tax due is smaller, so only {saving} KRW comes off. Unused credit is not carried forward.
status.full: Your tax falls by the {credit} KRW credit plus 10% local income tax.

threshold.title: 3% of gross pay threshold
threshold.short: {gap} KRW to go. Medical costs up to the 3% threshold are not credited.
threshold.over: You are {over} KRW over the threshold. Only the excess is credited.
threshold.more: Paying another {extraM}M KRW of medical costs by December 31 would cut your tax by a further {more} KRW.
threshold.moreZero: No tax is left to reduce, so extra medical costs would not lower your tax.

table.caption: 3% threshold deduction and creditable amount by type of medical cost
table.capped: Other family costs exceed the 7M KRW cap by {capped} KRW, and that part is not credited.
table.note: By law the 3% threshold comes off other family costs first, then your own and similar costs, then premature infant costs, then infertility treatment (Income Tax Act §59-4(2)). Costs are after insurance payouts.

share.label: Gross pay {salaryM}M KRW · medical costs {spentM}M KRW
share.headline: Tax down {saving} KRW
share.text: With gross pay of {salaryM}M KRW and {spentM}M KRW in medical costs, the medical expense credit is {credit} KRW and tax falls by {saving} KRW.

calendar.title: Last day to pay medical costs for this year's credit
calendar.note: Medical costs paid by December 31 count in this year's settlement. Recalculate on ToolHub: {url}

couple.title: Dual-income couple: who should pay and claim?
couple.desc: Each person's 3% threshold comes from their own gross pay, so the lower earner has a lower threshold. But credit larger than the tax due is lost, so both people's tax has to be calculated together.
couple.spouseSalaryHint: Enter it to compare all eight splits
couple.spouseOwnHint: What your spouse paid for their own care (after insurance)
couple.empty: Enter your spouse's gross pay to see who should pay your costs, your spouse's costs and family costs so that your combined tax falls the most.
couple.best: Splitting it this way cuts your tax by another {gain} KRW
couple.same: Keeping it as it is (you pay family costs) is best

table.caption: Tax reduction for each person by split of medical costs

couple.note: Calculated from gross pay alone, assuming neither of you has other deductions (incl. local income tax). Card, insurance or child deductions lower the tax due and can change the result, so check each of you in the year-end tax calculator.

rules.title: Which medical costs can move between spouses
items: The credit goes to the worker who actually paid (Enforcement Decree §118-5). Costs already paid cannot be moved, so use this to decide whose card or account pays for the rest of the year.

Your spouse's medical costs can be claimed by whoever paid them, whatever your spouse earns. In your settlement, however, your spouse is not 'you', so the costs fall under other family with the 7M KRW cap (no cap if your spouse is 65+ or disabled).

Children's and parents' medical costs count only if paid by the person who claims that family member as a basic deduction. If the husband claims the child and the wife pays the child's hospital bill, the wife cannot claim it.
Parents who cannot be claimed because they earn over 1M KRW a year or are under 60 still count if you support them and nobody else claims them. Siblings must live at the same registered address.
Moving a child's basic deduction also moves the 1.5M KRW personal deduction, the child tax credit and education credits. Check the full effect for each of you in the year-end tax calculator.

items.title: What counts as a medical expense

rows.item: Hospital, dental and Korean medicine clinic fees, inpatient care, health checkups
rows.note: Diagnosis, treatment and prevention at medical institutions under the Medical Service Act (Enforcement Decree §118-5(1)1)

rows.item: Medicines for treatment or recuperation (incl. herbal medicine)
rows.note: Pharmacy purchases count if for treatment; tonics for general health do not (§118-5(1)2, (2))
Up to 500,000 KRW per person a year (§118-5(1)4)

rows.item: LASIK and other vision correction surgery
rows.note: Surgery fees paid to a medical institution count (NTS help center)

rows.item: Assistive devices for the disabled, prescribed medical devices (purchase or rental)
rows.note: Medical devices need a doctor's prescription (§118-5(1)3)
Up to 2M KRW per birth; no gross pay limit for costs paid from 2024 (§118-5(1)7)

rows.item: Co-payments for long-term care and disability activity support
rows.note: Co-payments actually paid; activity support from 2024 (§118-5(1)6, 6-2)

rows.item: Infertility treatment and related prescription drugs
Health supplements and tonics for general health
rows.note: Not medicines, or for general health (§118-5(2), NTS help center)
Not payment for medical services (NTS help center)
Foreign hospitals are not medical institutions under the Medical Service Act (NTS help center)

rows.item: Amounts refunded by indemnity insurance or the out-of-pocket ceiling scheme
Costs paid before you joined or after you left your job
rows.note: Only costs paid while employed (incl. leave) count (NTS help center)

missing.title: Costs missing from the simplified data and receipts
items: Sellers of glasses, contact lenses and hearing aids do not have to submit data (Enforcement Decree §216-3), so these may not appear. Ask the store for a receipt with the user's name and give it to your employer.
For assistive devices and medical devices, keep the purchase or rental receipt, plus the prescription for medical devices.
If a postpartum care center is missing, ask it for a receipt showing the user's name and the amount.

If hospital or pharmacy data is missing or wrong, report it to the missing medical expense center after the service opens on January 15; if it still does not appear, get a payment certificate from the hospital.
Data for parents and adult children appears only after they consent to share it on Hometax.
Insurance payouts also appear in the simplified data. If you claimed a cost and were reimbursed the next year, the credit for the year you paid must be corrected.

refund.title: Missed it? Claim it back within five years
items: During the May income tax filing period, go to Hometax [Tax return] → [Comprehensive income tax] → [Earned income return] → [Regular return], load your year-end settlement and add the missing costs.
After May, use the request for correction (gyeongjeong cheonggu) in the same menu. The screen for the previous tax year usually opens around July.

The deadline is five years from the settlement tax payment date (usually March 10 of the following year) under Framework Act on National Taxes §45-2(5). Right now you can still claim back to the {old} tax year (until March 10, {until}).
Attach the receipts or the hospital's payment certificate. The tax office must reply within two months of receiving the request (§45-2(3)).

yearEnd.title: Year-end tax calculator
yearEnd.desc: Calculate your whole refund with these medical costs included

card.title: Credit card deduction
card.desc: Medical costs paid by card also count as card spending (both apply)

rent.title: Monthly rent tax credit
rent.desc: 15–17% of rent for non-homeowners earning up to 80M KRW

pension.title: Pension savings and IRP credit
pension.desc: 12–15% of up to 9M KRW paid in by December 31

medicalTaxCredit.source: Basis: Income Tax Act §59-4(2), Enforcement Decree §118-5, NTS help center medical expense Q&A · tax year {year} (laws in force as of October 2026)
